slides.0.title: Three Climate Zones and Topographic Influence
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 1 · Lesson 3
slides.1.title: Australia's Three Major Climate Types
slides.1.points.0: 🌊 Maritime / Cool: Tasmania, Mornington Peninsula, Margaret River — coastal sea breezes and low temperatures
slides.1.points.1: 🌤️ Mediterranean: Adelaide Hills, McLaren Vale, Margaret River — warm dry summers, mild winters
slides.1.points.2: 🌡️ Continental / Hot: Barossa Valley, Riverland, Murray Darling — extreme temperature variation, high heat
slides.1.note: The ocean's cooling influence can reach dozens of kilometres inland — key for understanding regional differences
slides.2.title: How Altitude Affects Wine
slides.2.points.0: Every 100 m increase in altitude ≈ 0.6–1°C temperature drop
slides.2.points.1: 🏔️ Adelaide Hills (400–700 m): cool-climate Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir
slides.2.points.2: 🏔️ Granite Belt QLD (900–1,100 m): Queensland's only cool-climate wine region
slides.2.points.3: 🏔️ Orange NSW (600–1,000 m): famous for cool-climate Chardonnay and Pinot Gris
slides.2.points.4: High altitude = longer ripening period = more nuanced aromas and higher acidity
slides.3.title: Four Key Cooling Mechanisms
slides.3.points.0: 🌊 Ocean Breeze: Margaret River, McLaren Vale — cool sea air reduces afternoon temperatures
slides.3.points.1: 🏔️ Altitude: Adelaide Hills, Orange, Granite Belt — cold air at elevation slows ripening
slides.3.points.2: ❄️ Southern Ocean: Tasmania — cold Antarctic currents maintain consistent low temperatures
slides.3.points.3: 🌙 Diurnal Range: Coonawarra, Clare Valley — large day/night temperature swings preserve acidity and aromatics
slides.4.question: Why can Margaret River in Western Australia produce premium cool-climate wines despite being relatively northerly?
slides.4.options.0: The region is at very high altitude
slides.4.options.1: The Indian Ocean and Southern Ocean converge nearby, bringing constant cooling sea breezes
slides.4.explanation: Margaret River sits at the tip of the South-West of WA, where the Indian and Southern Oceans meet. This generates cool maritime sea breezes that moderate temperatures and extend the growing season — perfect for Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: Three climate types: maritime/cool, Mediterranean, continental/hot — each produces distinct wine styles
slides.5.points.1: Altitude is the key cool-climate tool: Adelaide Hills, Orange, Granite Belt are prime examples
slides.5.points.2: Four cooling mechanisms: ocean breeze, altitude, Southern Ocean, diurnal range
